# Kite

> HTML is enough for small things.

Kite is a teaching toolkit for building small, self-contained interactive web apps using only HTML and CSS.

## Not a framework

Kite is not React, Vue, or Svelte. It is not for production-scale systems or large multi-team codebases. See https://getkite.netlify.app/docs/1-basics/limits.md for honest constraints (<500 interactive nodes, <20 models).

## Quick start

```html
<script src="https://esm.sh/@kitelet/core"></script>

<div kite-scope="{ count: 0 }">
  <button kite-on-click="count++">+1</button>
  <span kite-text="count"></span>
</div>
```

## Core concepts

- Directives: declarative `kite-*` attributes (`kite-scope`, `kite-text`, `kite-model`, `kite-for`, `kite-if`, `kite-on-*`)
- Components: declarative `<kite-component>` templates instantiated via `<kite-use>` with slots and props
- MVCR Architecture: `<kite-model>`, `<kite-view>`, `<kite-controller>`, `<kite-route>` directly in native HTML
- API: `<kite-api>` client definitions with protocol adapters

## Agentic Metadata

- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): Agent entry point and onboarding instructions
- [.kite/capabilities.json](.kite/capabilities.json): Machine-readable signatures for every directive, tag, API, helper
- [.kite/rules.json](.kite/rules.json): Machine-checkable constraints and severity definitions
- [.kite/conventions.json](.kite/conventions.json): 9-slot markup order and file naming standards
- [.kite/limits.json](.kite/limits.json): Scale constraints and graduation triggers
